premise: 1884, a fictional Colorado railway town. A freight receipt conflicts with a station timetable. Procedural frontier investigation with outdoor pursuit; firearms and horses are not automatically granted.

history.scope: Prior background-chargen review read the 1883 standard-time and telegraph discussion. On 2026-09-06 current search returned relevant excerpts, direct article access returned 403; alternative LOC guide returned 429. Current pack does not claim fresh full-text access. The town, wiring, local clock disagreement and access permissions are original assumptions; no exact offset or price is inferred.

items.name: Station message copy
items.acquisition: Optional equipment supplied at the relevant scene by its fictional custodian; not added to starting cards.
items.price_basis: Explicit loan or supply allocation, no purchase or historically asserted price.
items.procedure: Compare the sender, recipient and time notation with a permitted station log.
items.effect: Shows the recorded message exactly as supplied; no guarantee it is truthful.
items.limits: One employer-provided copy; access covers this message only.
items.upkeep: Keep dry; if damaged, request a clerk's recollection at a delay cost.
items.substitute: Ask the clerk to identify the destination and uncertainty orally.

items.name: Track-inspection sketch
items.acquisition: Optional equipment supplied at the relevant scene by its fictional custodian; not added to starting cards.
items.price_basis: Explicit loan or supply allocation, no purchase or historically asserted price.
items.procedure: Mark a public inspection route and compare observed landmarks.
items.effect: Helps communicate locations; does not locate tracks or grant a Navigate bonus.
items.limits: One fictional employer sketch, not a surveyed map or travel ticket.
items.upkeep: Update only observed landmarks; replace through the station office.
items.substitute: Travel with the local inspector on the public path.

items.name: Repair kit
items.acquisition: Optional equipment supplied at the relevant scene by its fictional custodian; not added to starting cards.
items.price_basis: Explicit loan or supply allocation, no purchase or historically asserted price.
items.procedure: Inspect an isolated, nonoperating lock or latch with the owner's permission.
items.effect: Enables ordinary repair work under core skill rules; no automatic success or damage bonus.
items.limits: One loan; does not authorize railway operation, sabotage or work on moving equipment.
items.upkeep: Return parts after use; a missing part requires a station mechanic.
items.substitute: Have the authorized mechanic inspect it and report findings.

scenes.title: Station office
scenes.purpose: Separate time notation from the cargo allegation.
scenes.entry: Two clocks disagree with a handwritten receipt. Reach it through the preceding lead; the first scene is the agreed starting appointment.
scenes.exit_condition: Follow the next lead or leave with an explicitly incomplete report at the final scene.
scenes.npc: Clerk Mara wants the station cleared of theft accusations; she will explain log conventions but not release every message.
scenes.objects: Message copy, wall clock, freight destination list.
scenes.clue: The notation discrepancy points to the loading siding; it does not prove a theft.
scenes.pressure: Original shared delay counter starts at 0. Each failed specialist attempt or ordinary route adds 1; at the first total of 3 the primary NPC leaves. The named ordinary-route contact stays available. Further delays do not remove that contact. No automatic HP/SAN loss.

routes.method: Ask how the apparatus and log were used, then inspect a permitted connection.
routes.cost: One investigative attempt; on failure add one delay and use a different route or meet native-system retry conditions.
routes.outcome: Success: The notation discrepancy points to the loading siding; it does not prove a theft. Failure: A failed inspection delays confirmation; Mara names the siding but cannot vouch for the disputed timestamp.

routes.method: Negotiate the specific cooperation described in the NPC entry.
routes.cost: An interview and an offered favor; decline or failed persuasion leaves the ordinary route available.
routes.outcome: Success gains a more precise account with permission; failure withholds that cooperation, not every onward lead.

routes.method: Platform porter Ames orally reads the loading destination from the public freight notice: the siding. Ames remains on shift after Mara leaves; the disputed timestamp is not confirmed.
routes.cost: One delay; no special equipment or successful skill roll. Accept less precise evidence and the stated access limits.
routes.outcome: After a failed specialized attempt, take this separate limited lead and pay the ordinary delay. Platform porter Ames orally reads the loading destination from the public freight notice: the siding. Ames remains on shift after Mara leaves; the disputed timestamp is not confirmed.

scenes.title: Loading siding
scenes.purpose: Determine which route the wagon took.
scenes.entry: Crate splinters lie beside a public footpath. Reach it through the preceding lead; the first scene is the agreed starting appointment.
scenes.exit_condition: Follow the next lead or leave with an explicitly incomplete report at the final scene.
scenes.npc: Inspector Cole wants the line safe; he trades a guided look for an accurate damage report.
scenes.objects: Route sketch, wagon impressions, broken packing strip.
scenes.clue: A wagon proceeded to the inland storehouse, not the outbound platform.
scenes.pressure: Original shared delay counter starts at 0. Each failed specialist attempt or ordinary route adds 1; at the first total of 3 the primary NPC leaves. The named ordinary-route contact stays available. Further delays do not remove that contact. No automatic HP/SAN loss.

routes.method: Compare fresh impressions along the permitted path.
routes.cost: One investigative attempt; on failure add one delay and use a different route or meet native-system retry conditions.
routes.outcome: Success: A wagon proceeded to the inland storehouse, not the outbound platform. Failure: Wind obscures the marks; Cole offers a slower guided route without confirming the exact wagon.

routes.method: Negotiate the specific cooperation described in the NPC entry.
routes.cost: An interview and an offered favor; decline or failed persuasion leaves the ordinary route available.
routes.outcome: Success gains a more precise account with permission; failure withholds that cooperation, not every onward lead.

routes.method: Crossing attendant Beck describes the public path to the inland storehouse. Beck remains posted when Cole leaves; the route gives access without confirming which wagon made the tracks.
routes.cost: One delay; no special equipment or successful skill roll. Accept less precise evidence and the stated access limits.
routes.outcome: After a failed specialized attempt, take this separate limited lead and pay the ordinary delay. Crossing attendant Beck describes the public path to the inland storehouse. Beck remains posted when Cole leaves; the route gives access without confirming which wagon made the tracks.

scenes.title: Inland storehouse
scenes.entry: A strained latch catches on an uneven door. Reach it through the preceding lead; the first scene is the agreed starting appointment.
scenes.exit_condition: Follow the next lead or leave with an explicitly incomplete report at the final scene.
scenes.npc: Storekeeper Venn fears a negligence claim; he permits a witnessed inspection and can offer an oral account.
scenes.objects: Latch, packing list, signed arrival stub.
scenes.clue: The cargo remained inland during an unrecorded repair; responsibility depends on whose instructions were followed.
scenes.pressure: Original shared delay counter starts at 0. Each failed specialist attempt or ordinary route adds 1; at the first total of 3 the primary NPC leaves. The named ordinary-route contact stays available. Further delays do not remove that contact. No automatic HP/SAN loss.

routes.method: Inspect the idle latch with a mechanic and compare the arrival stub.
routes.cost: One investigative attempt; on failure add one delay and use a different route or meet native-system retry conditions.
routes.outcome: Success: The cargo remained inland during an unrecorded repair; responsibility depends on whose instructions were followed. Failure: Failure leaves the mechanical cause unresolved; the witnessed oral account still establishes where the cargo waited.

routes.method: Negotiate the specific cooperation described in the NPC entry.
routes.cost: An interview and an offered favor; decline or failed persuasion leaves the ordinary route available.
routes.outcome: Success gains a more precise account with permission; failure withholds that cooperation, not every onward lead.

routes.method: Relief worker Dale gives the public arrival time from the shift handover. Dale stays after Venn leaves; the party can report that cargo waited here while the mechanical cause remains unresolved.
routes.cost: One delay; no special equipment or successful skill roll. Accept less precise evidence and the stated access limits.
routes.outcome: After a failed specialized attempt, take this separate limited lead and pay the ordinary delay. Relief worker Dale gives the public arrival time from the shift handover.
